notes: TOSEMU is Johan Toverland Thelin’s hosted environment for original Atari TOS executables, not a decompilation of one guest application. The current PRG loader opens and maps the supplied file, checks magic 0x601A, constructs the guest environment and applies relocation entries. The tosemu executable runs a program directly; the separate tosaesd daemon supports shared GEM accessory sessions and is not a prerequisite for a single CLI invocation. README explicitly targets integration into Linux and excludes general games/demos. This repository is counted once; its hosted EmuTOS and Musashi components are dependencies, not additional runner discoveries. Canonical repository and lineage aliases were screened against the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and prior dedup index; no existing counted project matched. Source snapshot 443340b2dfcf9e691a080bc4e3722102bc9c2839, non-truncated tree with 274 entries. Tooling: original-binary CPU emulation plus TOS system-call reimplementation. src/musashi.c intercepts traps 1, 2, 13 and 14 for GEMDOS, GEM, BIOS and XBIOS, while src/gemdosfile.c maps guest file reads to host stdio and copies data into emulated memory. The guest instructions still execute in Musashi; native host API handling does not make the guest a source port or ahead-of-time translation. Hosted EmuTOS AES/VDI routines supply graphical APIs without booting an Atari ROM. Terminal usage, headless support and self-hosted retro development tests establish the requested runner category, without implying complete TOS or ST hardware compatibility. The guest ISA is Motorola 68000: tossystem.c selects M68K_CPU_TYPE_68000 and musashiconf.h disables later 68010/020/030/040 processors and the PMMU. Original .TTP/.TOS/.PRG guest binaries and TOS belong in source_platforms/source_cpu. The Musashi package’s broader M680x0 support is not TOSEMU support for those later guest CPUs. The FPU entry stubs abort and are not an emulated FPU. Neither the build’s __mcoldfire__ adaptation define nor EmuTOS source ancestry establishes a ColdFire host target. Linux is the explicit host target, but the inspected host Makefile and Ubuntu workflow do not establish a host ISA support matrix or minimum processor. target_cpu remains empty. GCC, C source, -no-pie, 32-bit GEM pointer fields and ubuntu-latest are not sufficient to label x86-64, ARM or another host architecture. The EmuTOS __mcoldfire__ define is a source-adaptation switch selecting portable C rather than a claim that the runnable host program targets ColdFire. README requires recursive Musashi and EmuTOS submodules and make; Makefile uses GCC, generates Musashi opcode tables and links hosted EmuTOS AES/VDI. NO_WAYLAND=1 removes the Wayland/xkbcommon headers, libraries and protocol-generation route; the Ubuntu workflow explicitly uses it for check and emuvdi-check. The GUI route needs Wayland tooling; optional detected integrations include D-Bus, libpng, FreeType/fontconfig and ALSA. The hosted EmuTOS build uses -fno-strict-aliasing and non-PIE flags because guest APIs contain 32-bit pointer fields. Devpac/Lattice tests are separate from building the host runner and require the original installations. Upstream describes excluding SoftFloat and dead-stripping unused later-CPU FPU/MMU code; this review did not inspect a resulting binary or certify link-time license composition. All four build flags remain null; inspected recipes and upstream reports are not local test results. A Linux terminal/headless host profile is documented: tosemu PROGRAM.TTP [arguments], TOSEMU_CONSOLE=terminal and TOSEMU_NO_WINDOW=1; make NO_WAYLAND=1 supports a host build without the graphical dependency. No desktop session or accessory daemon is needed for ordinary CLI execution. No verified CPU, OS-version, RAM or chipset minimum is stated, so none is populated. TOSEMU_MEMORY is guest memory configuration, not a host-RAM minimum. Windows and macOS are not asserted. Host filesystem access is direct: C: defaults to the host root, while TOS_BASE_PATH relocates it and rejects paths resolving outside that base; this is a path-mapping feature, not a demonstrated security sandbox. TOS basepage arguments have a 126-character limit, with the ARGV convention retained for cooperating programs. README explicitly acknowledges use of LLM technology. TOSEMU’s COPYING carries GPLv2 and source headers allow v2 or later; Musashi has its permissive MIT-like grant, and the hosted EmuTOS documentation records its GPL lineage. README/Makefile explicitly distinguish bundled later-CPU SoftFloat/MAME code from what upstream says is linked, so redistribution still needs the actual chosen build/dependency licenses checked. notes: Identity: Miro Kropacek/MiKRO identifies uDump 1.03 as a TOS ROM dumping utility for ST, STE, TT and Falcon. The entire five-file tree contains its C implementation, build recipe, author README and license; this is the canonical non-fork repository. Classification: A native preservation tool that obtains the TOS header, identifies version/country and machine cookies, selects ROM size and writes a named image. It handles EmuTOS and CT60 cases and copies ROM through a bounded buffer to avoid a documented extra-read bus error. It does not reconstruct or emulate TOS execution. Source CPU: uDump copies ROM bytes and parses header/cookie metadata rather than disassembling or interpreting the captured instructions. The ROM platform is recorded, but no original CPU analysis is claimed. Target CPU: Makefile uses m68k-atari-mint-gcc with explicit -m68000 and links libcmini startup/runtime into udump.tos. This establishes a native Motorola 68000 target without implying that all supported Atari models have the same minimum RAM or firmware. Build: The Makefile declares a libcmini-based native .tos build. The creator publishes a uDump 1.03 binary archive and earlier release notes explicitly discuss the distributed executable; runnable=true records that released utility, not a local run. The current source build was not reproduced, so compilable remains null and no gameplay or historical byte-match claim is made. Limitations: No cross-compilation, execution, real-machine ROM capture or binary comparison was performed. Runtime profiles: README names ST/STE/TT/Falcon and the source selects TOS ROM sizes and CT60/EmuTOS variants, but it does not specify a complete minimum-memory or OS-version configuration. The 16 KiB transfer buffer and -m68000 flag do not establish a runtime minimum. AI: The full five-file inventory, README, C implementation, Makefile and all 12 returned commits show no explicit generative-AI development disclosure. Usage is unknown, including later maintenance of the historical code.
